title: A Measurement Invariance Study of the Sexual Cognitions Checklist Across Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity.
abstract: The Sexual Cognitions Checklist (SCC) provides a unique framework for assessing both positive (PSC) and negative sexual cognitions (NSC). Few studies have examined sexual fantasies and cognitions in sexual orientation and gender diversity (SOGD) populations. This study tested the measurement invariance, reliability, and validity of the Spanish SCC scores across sexual orientation and gender identity groups. Using a nationwide strategy, a sample of 2,000 adults was recruited: 443 bisexual, 693 gay, and 829 heterosexual individuals; by gender, there were 963 cisgender men, 856 cisgender women, and 181 transgender and gender-diverse (TGD) individuals. Results supported strict or partial strict invariance for both positive and negative subscales (SCC-PSC and SCC-NSC), supporting meaningful cross-group comparisons. Significant differences emerged across sexual orientation and gender identity in PSC and NSC dimensions. PSC showed the most consistent associations, in a positive direction, with self-reported sexual functioning (i.e., desire, arousal, and penile erection/vaginal lubrication), whereas NSC showed fewer, negative associations. These findings address a critical gap by including underrepresented populations and extending the evidence base beyond cisgender heterosexual samples. To our knowledge, the SCC is currently the only instrument in the Spanish context with psychometric evidence supporting its use across SOGD groups, making it a potentially valuable tool for inclusive research and clinical practice in sexual health.
